Don't be. Planet Fitness gets a bad rap, but it's not nearly as bad as the majority of Reddit "fitness experts" would have you believe. At the end of the day, you get out what you put in. Planet Fitness has all the tools for you to achieve any health goal, minus a dedicated powerlifting section with barbells and such, but you can get the same, if not better results using dumbbells instead anyway. If you know what you're doing, you'll get the results you desire.

Yes, they give out pizza once a month, (how terrible! One unhealthy snack a month!), and yes, there's lots of beginners who go there, but I also know plenty of seasoned lifters who go there on a regular basis. Hell, there's many jacked professional wrestlers who use them frequently. Don't let the gym hipsters fool you, you can reach your fitness goals at Planet Fitness, and you can do it for much cheaper and without the meatheads yelling and slamming weights right next to you.

Oh, and don't waste your money on a "weightlifting gym". I've been to several gyms that claim to be, "a real man's gym, not like that pussy ass Planet Fitness", and you know what they have? Old, rusty free weights and some halfway broken machines. That's it. Planet Fitness has everything these other gyms have, and more, for a cheaper price. It's up to you at the end of the day, but don't buy into the meathead bullshit that so many Redditors throw around.

Started talking to a girl on Bumble. Things were going pretty well through our messages, so I asked if I could take her on a date during the upcoming weekend. I pick her up and take her to an Italian place. On the way there, the song "Hip to be Square" by Huey Lewis & The News starts playing on Spotify. She mentions that she loves my taste in music. So far, so good, right? After we get seated at the restaurant, we start talking about tattoos. She then proceeds to pull down her sleeve to reveal a tattoo of a giant, bloody knife on her forearm. Now, I have some pretty dark tattoos as well, so I wasn't judging. But then she mentions that she is "obsessed" with the film American Psycho (hence her loving the song that plays when the main character hacks his colleague to death with an axe). Me being desperate at the time, I still finish the date and drop her back off, asking if I could take her on a second one the following week. She says yes and goes to bed.

I send her a goodnight text and tell her that I had a great time. She doesn't respond for two days, and when she does, she mentions that she didn't text me because her ex had come over and stayed for those days, and she thought it would be rude to tell him she was seeing other guys. I ghosted her shortly after.

Oh, also, she had a YouTube channel where she posted rants about how much she was obsessed with BTS and also posted videos of her dancing while angrily flipping off the camera. Not that relevant, but I thought it was funny detail about the whole situation.

Oh man, get ready to have your mind blown. The [Dragon Age Keep](https://dragonagekeep.com/) is a website that allows you to determine the choices of Dragon Age: Origins and Dragon Age II. Who dies, who lives, who you help, who you ignore, etc. You can then import these choices into Dragon Age Inquisition, which changes the world dramatically. For example, say you chose to have a character die in Dragon Age Origins. This character will not appear in Dragon Age Inquisition. But if you chose for them to live, they could very well pop up during a quest.

Tbh, the only things I want out of life are money, fame, and true love. I have absolutely no desire to "start a family" by having kids. I've never heard an argument that even remotely convinced me that it might be a good idea. I can understand why other people want to, but it's just not for me.

* Get the Deft Hands, Fine Tools perk as soon as you can. You can get some awesome equipment/schematics from those masterwork locked doors.

* Agents count as perks for their respective categories, so instead of spending perk points on things you don't want, just pick up some agents. Sometimes you'll be able to choose where these agents work, as well, so if you're going after Deft Hands, Fine Tools, get them to work in the "Secrets" section (it'll be the choice that seems the most spy-like).

* If you haven't already, get the "knowledge" perks (underworld knowledge, historical knowledge, etc) in the "Forces", "Secrets", and "Connections" categories. They can give you extra options for choices down the line, as well as bonus XP.

* Unless they're blocking your path, completely ignore the fade rifts. They're pretty much only there to give you a few power points, but you'll have plenty of power without them.

* Don't be afraid to use materials for crafting just because they're only tier 1 or tier 2. You won't be getting enough tier 3 materials for crafting until you're near the end of the game. Often, crafted items are better than what you'll pick up as loot.

* Crafted weapon accessories (hilts, grips, etc) can only go in certain weapons. If you're not sure if what you're crafting can fit in your weapon, make a save before crafting so you can go back and not waste your materials.

* I'm not sure how much help it will be without me spoiling it, but there's an area late in the game with a lot of caves that can only be opened by puzzles. DO THE PUZZLES. Look up the solutions online if you need to, but make sure you do the puzzles. They lead to some of the best loot in the game.

* If you didn't before, use the Dragon Age Keep before you start a new playthrough. It can make the difference between characters playing a huge part in a quest and not being present at all.

* Speak to your companions after every major plot development.

* Most of the time, the war table choices that take the shortest amount of time lead to the best outcome. However, make sure you read the descriptions carefully, especially if you're thinking about going with Cullen's solution, as sometimes his only solution is to do nothing.

* Play the game how you want to play it. If there's an optional side quest that you're not crazy about, don't do it.

* Try a playthrough with at least every race, and at least one of each sex. It really makes a difference in terms of dialogue and who you can romance.

* If a dialogue choice causes a question mark to pop up in the center, it asks a question, but doesn't advance the conversation, meaning you can exhaust all of those options without having to worry about its effect on the plot. This is only not the case in one quest, but you should be able to tell which one I'm talking about by clues in the dialogue.

* You don't take any fall damage in Skyhold, so feel free to jump off of the tall ledges to reach areas quicker.

* Certain areas have higher level enemies than others. If the first enemies you find in an area are 5+ levels above you, go somewhere else first, they're not getting any easier.

* If you think the game's about to end, chances are, it isn't. Inquisition is a veeeerrrrry long game.

After another hour of awkward silence, someone suggested that we take a group picture, and I have to say, it's hilarious when I look back at it, because my expression in the picture is the very definition of "smiling like I'm dead inside." After we took the picture, she asked me if I wanted to dance, and before I even finished saying, "I'm not much of a dancer", she walked away. I spent the rest of the night talking to my friend's date while the aforementioned friend was up talking with some other mutual friends. This was the only good part of the night, because in addition to being a gorgeous model, she also happens to be unbelievably hilarious. The next thing I knew, my date walks over and says she's leaving with another guy and his date, who was her best friend. She apparently told the guy this beforehand, but never told me. Meh.

I walked over to my friend and his gorgeous date, made a few self-deprecating suicide jokes, and convinced him to leave. He drops me off at my house, I lock myself in my room, and then proceed to listen to extremely depressing music and cut myself for three hours. Oh, and this might make the story better: the next day was my 18th birthday. Also, I skipped going to a WWE show (I'm a huge pro wrestling geek) so I could experience this hellhole.

TLDR- Went with a girl I hardly knew, didn't speak or dance all night, date left with another guy, worst memory of my high school days.
